brief: A kitchen herb planter: two or three bins on a base, filled with soil and planted with basil and thyme.

requirements.requirement: Two or three bins on a base
requirements.evidence: Build has 3 full hex bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full) in L-shape with 3 full-depth bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full. Joints locked and open faces capped.
All three bins filled with soil to rim (soil entries for each bin: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full).
Two bins planted with basil-young plugs (prop:1 in bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and prop:3 in bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full), visible in look view.
One bin planted with thyme-young plug (prop:2 in bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full), visible in look view.

finish.summary: Built compact L-shaped kitchen herb planter with 3 hex bases and 3 full-depth bins, all filled with soil and planted: basil in two bins and thyme in one. House rules applied (capOpenFaces, lockJoints), check_build clear with no mesh clash.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
